1 ἐν τάχει ('in haste') the codex has, corrected by Kroll. 10 τρίτον ('third') I have written, γὰρ ('for') the codex has from γ´, as it seems, wrongly
understood 12 ἅπερ ('which things') the codex has. 14 αὐτ’ ('it') the codex has, αὑτοῦ ('of himself') I have written and bracketed, “ perhaps to be de-
leted ” Kroll. 17 πόλεως ('of the city') the codex has, πόρνης ('of a prostitute') conjectured by Kroll. 19 ἐν μεσουρανήματι ('in midheaven') I sup-
plied. 21 ἅτερ ('without') the codex has. 22 I have marked a lacuna ; mention of Hermes is missing. δὲ ('but') I supplied.
ἀποτέλεσμενα ('outcome' [corrupt]) the codex has, ἀποτέλεσμα ('outcome') I have written. 27 αὐτὲ δι’ ἑαυτ’ ἐρωτησ´ ('he himself through himself asked' [corrupt]) the codex has, αὐτὸς
δι’ ἑαυτου κινδυνεύσει ('he himself through himself will be in danger') I have written. 32-33 ἀπηνεγκατος <sic> ('carried off' [corrupt]) the codex has. πρὸς ('towards') added by Kroll.
35 τὸ ὑπόγειον ('the subterranean') understand δηλοῖ ('it signifies').

summary.headline: Astrology of the Fugitive
summary.text: Astrological rules for judging a fugitive’s return, duration of absence, motive, punishment, and possessions from the zodiac signs and the planets in the ascendant, midheaven, setting, and subterranean position. Aries through Pisces are interpreted alongside Saturn, Mars, Jupiter, Venus, and Mercury.
